thread.title: Ann Arbor community members protest gender-affirming care cuts
thread.title_full: Ann Arbor community members protest gender-affirming care cuts

author: Glenn Hedin
title: Ann Arbor community members protest gender-affirming care cuts
text:
On Wednesday afternoon, more than a hundred people gathered inside the D. Dan and Betty Kahn Health Care Pavilion — Michigan Medicine’s newest hospital — to celebrate its grand opening. The atmosphere inside was one of celebration. The new hospital, an addition to University of Michigan’s medical complex that spans 12 stories and 690,000 square feet, contains advanced specialty care services for individuals suffering from neurological and cardiovascular conditions.
Separated by a wall of glass windows, a group of Ann Arbor residents protested a few feet away from the building to remind attendees of Michigan Medicine’s decision to cease providing gender-affirming care to individuals under the age of 19 in response to a subpoena from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
In an interview with The Michigan Daily, Lauren Gaboury, an organizer with the Huron Valley Democratic Socialists of America who helped organize the rally, said they believed the opening ceremony’s congratulatory atmosphere was hypocritical.
“They claim to be the Leaders and the Best, but they’re not leading or being the best on the topic of gender-affirming care,” Gaboury said.
In an email to The Daily, Mary Masson, Michigan Medicine public relations director, wrote that Michigan Medicine has worked to support former recipients of gender-affirming care. The statement was nearly identical to an email sent by Masson to The Daily following a previous protest for gender-affirming care in September.
“We recognize the gravity and impact of our recent decision to discontinue pediatric gender affirming care for our patients and our community,” Masson wrote. “We have worked closely with and will continuously support the well-being of our patients, their families, and our care teams.”
Masson also wrote that Michigan Medicine is grateful to its physicians for their willingness to provide high-quality care to all their patients.
“We are deeply grateful to our clinicians for their unyielding commitment to providing the highest quality care, and to all of our team members for their dedication to helping our patients, and to supporting each other, as we navigate these changes together,” Masson wrote.
Activists outside the hospital had a different perspective. Gaboury said they and the other demonstrators were frustrated at the disparity between the amount of resources spent on the new hospital, contrasted with the lack of support Michigan Medicine has given to individuals who require gender-affirming care.
“These cuts have been devastating to thousands of patients in the area, both in and out of state,” Gaboury said. “And now (the University) is opening their long awaited wing of the hospital for $920 million, and they’re not using any of those resources to protect and defend the care that they were providing from the federal government.”
Gaboury said they believed the University’s acquiescence to the federal government will enable future repressive measures against other marginalized groups.
“The federal government will continue to try to erode rights,” Gaboury said. “It’ll be trans kids first. Then it’ll be trans adults. Next, it’ll be abortion care. And, this is just the beginning, so the fact that (the University) has already rolled over on this leaves everybody else vulnerable as well.”
Gaboury said they wished Michigan Medicine would allow its clinicians to provide high-quality gender-affirming care to transgender youth through other institutions that have not yet banned the practice by releasing its clinical staff from noncompetition agreements.
“There are Michigan Medicine providers who want to keep continuing gender-affirming care, but they are now being prevented from doing that by their employer,” Gaboury said. “One of the things that (the University) could do would be to release those providers from their noncompete contracts, to allow them to provide gender-affirming care elsewhere in other institutions that are still allowing this type of care.”
While activists held up signs that read “Protect trans kids” and “Whose care will you sacrifice next?” to the hospital’s windows, the opening ceremony continued uninterrupted. In a speech to ceremony attendees, University Regent Michael Behm (D) said he believes the new facility demonstrates Michigan Medicine’s leading position in the field of health care.
“When someone needs exceptional health care, whether they live in Ann Arbor, across the state or the region, they look to Michigan,” Behm said. “They know that it’s a place where medical care, training, research and innovation are world-class. With the addition of the D. Dan and Betty Kahn Health Care Pavilion, our health system will reach even more people and be able to care for them in an incredible facility.”
Kami Michels, a pro-gender-affirming care activist who was inside the building listening to Behm’s speech, told The Daily she appreciated Michigan Medicine’s construction of new medical facilities, but it did not make up for how they have treated transgender youth.
“I think that overall (Behm’s statement) — it used to be even more true until they decided to deprive transgender children of their care,” Michels said. “I think it’s wonderful that they have this new facility; I think that’s all great. But I also see their shame and cowardice, and I think Michigan Medicine are not the Leaders and the Best for all people.”
Daily Staff Reporter Glenn Hedin can be reached at heglenn@umich.edu.
